name: The Wheel
summary: A repeating cycle: sell cash-secured puts until shares are acquired, then sell covered calls against the shares until they are called away, then start again.

legs.strike_rule: phase 2: shares acquired at the put strike (or deliberately bought in the market)
phase 3: 0.25-0.30 delta covered call, strike >= share basis

max_profit: per cycle: put credits + call credits + (call strike - share basis) x 100; unbounded over many cycles
max_loss: (share basis - cumulative credits) x 100 if the underlying collapses while shares are held
breakevens: rolling: share basis minus all credits collected since inception

greeks.delta: +25 in the put phase, +70 in the covered call phase

when_to_use: On liquid, fundamentally acceptable underlyings the system is content to own for months - large-cap ETFs and blue chips. Requires IV Rank >= 30 to be worth the capital. Do NOT wheel high-beta names that can gap 40%.
entry_rules: Universe filter: price between $20 and $150 (so one lot is affordable in a $50k account), ADV >= 2M shares, weekly options available, OI >= 500, IV Rank >= 30, no binary catalysts.
Phase 1: standard CSP entry rules; cash reserved for the full strike.
Phase 3: standard covered call rules with the ADDITIONAL hard constraint strike >= share basis (basis = put strike - all credits collected to date).
Never run more than 3 wheels concurrently at $50k equity; total assignment notional <= 60% of equity.
Track a per-underlying ledger: cumulative credits, current basis, cycle count.
management_rules: Every short option: 50% profit target, 21 DTE close-or-roll.
Phase transition on purpose, never by accident: when the put goes ITM, close it and decide explicitly whether to buy the shares in the market at the prevailing price.
If shares are held and the stock falls > 15% below basis, keep writing calls but at the basis strike even if that is a low delta; do not write below basis to chase premium.
If the effective basis (after credits) falls below the current price, a call written at the strike just above basis is acceptable to exit the cycle.
Halt the wheel on an underlying after 4 consecutive losing cycles or a 25% drawdown from basis.
exit_rules: HARD, both phases: no ITM short leg is ever carried past 15:30 ET on expiration day. Put phase - close and buy shares deliberately if wanted. Call phase - close and sell shares deliberately if exiting.
Extrinsic guard on both phases: close when extrinsic < 0.05 and |delta| > 0.85.
Ex-dividend guard in the call phase: close or roll the day before ex-date if the call is ITM and extrinsic < 1.10 x dividend.
Cycle kill: if the underlying's thesis breaks (index deletion, halt, going-concern news), close options first, then liquidate shares.
assignment_risk: Both phases have an assignable short leg. The traditional wheel WANTS assignment; this system does not, and instead replicates the phase transition with explicit share orders. That distinction must be encoded: the wheel's state machine advances on the system's own share purchase, not on a broker assignment notice. Reconciliation logic must still handle an unexpected assignment (random OCC allocation) by re-syncing the ledger and share count.
buying_power: Put phase: strike x 100 in cash. Call phase: the shares. Effectively the full lot notional is committed for the whole cycle.
liquidity_needs: Both puts and calls liquid at 0.25-0.30 delta across weeklies and monthlies; OI >= 500.
common_mistakes: Wheeling a declining stock and calling the accumulated losses 'income'; writing calls below basis after a drawdown and locking the loss in; forgetting that the wheel is a covered strangle with extra steps and the same tail risk; running too many wheels for the account size.
zero_dte_notes: The wheel's economics depend on 30-45 DTE theta and on being willing to hold shares; a 0DTE wheel is just daily overwriting plus daily put writing (see those entries).
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
